macros.name: beginpgfgraphicnamed
macros.doc: This command indicates that everything up to the next call of \endpgfgraphicnamed is part of a graphic that should be placed in a file named ⟨file name prefix⟩.⟨suffix⟩, where the ⟨suffix⟩ depends on your backend driver.

macros.name: endpgfgraphicnamed
macros.doc: This command just marks the end of the graphic that should be externalized.

macros.name: pgfaliasid
macros.doc: Creates an alias of a name inside the current TeX scope.

macros.name: pgfaliasimage
macros.doc: The {⟨existing image name⟩} is “cloned” and the {⟨new image name⟩} can now be used whenever the original image is used.

macros.name: pgfalternateextension
macros.doc: If the macro \pgfalternateextension expands to some nonempty ⟨alternate extension⟩, pgf will first try to use the image named ⟨image name⟩.⟨alternate extension⟩.

macros.name: pgfclearid
macros.doc: Clears the current id (and type) for the local scope.

macros.name: pgfdeclarearrow
macros.doc: This command is both used to define a new arrow tip kind and to to declare a so-called shorthand.

macros.name: pgfdeclarefading
macros.doc: This command declares a fading named ⟨name⟩ for later use.

arg.snippet: pgfdeclarefunctionalshading[${1:color list}]{${2:shading name}}{${3:lower left corner}}{${4:upper right corner}}{${5:init code}}{${6:type 4 function}}
pgfdeclarefunctionalshading{${1:shading name}}{${2:lower left corner}}{${3:upper right corner}}{${4:init code}}{${5:type 4 function}}

macros.name: pgfdeclareimage
macros.doc: Declares an image, but does not paint anything.

macros.name: pgfdeclareimage
macros.doc: Declares an image, but does not paint anything.

macros.name: pgfdeclarelayer
macros.doc: This command declares a layer named ⟨name⟩ for later use.

macros.name: pgfdeclaremask
macros.doc: Declares a transparency mask named ⟨mask name⟩ (called a soft mask in the pdf specification).

macros.name: pgfdeclaremask
macros.doc: Declares a transparency mask named ⟨mask name⟩ (called a soft mask in the pdf specification).

macros.name: pgfextractx
macros.doc: Sets the TeX-⟨dimension⟩ to the x-coordinate of the point.

macros.name: pgffuncshadingcmyktogray
macros.doc: Within the ⟨type 4 function⟩ argument of \pgfdeclarefunctionalshading, this command can be used to convert the top 4 elements on the stack from cmyk to grayscale.

macros.name: pgffuncshadingcmyktorgb
macros.doc: Within the ⟨type 4 function⟩ argument of \pgfdeclarefunctionalshading, this command can be used to convert the top 4 elements on the stack from cmyk to rgb.

macros.name: pgffuncshadinggraytocmyk
macros.doc: Within the ⟨type 4 function⟩ argument of \pgfdeclarefunctionalshading, this command can be used to convert the top element on the stack from grayscale to cmyk.

macros.name: pgffuncshadinggraytorgb
macros.doc: Within the ⟨type 4 function⟩ argument of \pgfdeclarefunctionalshading, this command can be used to convert the top element on the stack from grayscale to rgb.

macros.name: pgffuncshadingrgbtocmyk
macros.doc: Within the ⟨type 4 function⟩ argument of \pgfdeclarefunctionalshading, this command can be used to convert the top 3 elements on the stack from rgb to cmyk.

macros.name: pgffuncshadingrgbtogray
macros.doc: Within the ⟨type 4 function⟩ argument of \pgfdeclarefunctionalshading, this command can be used to convert the top 3 elements on the stack from rgb to grayscale.

macros.name: pgfgetlastxy
macros.doc: Stores the most recently used (x, y) coordinates into two macros.

macros.name: pgfgettransform
macros.doc: This command will (locally) define ⟨macro⟩ to a representation of the current coordinate transformation matrix.

arg.snippet: pgfgettransformentries{${1:macro for a}}{${2:macro for b}}{${3:macro for c}}{${4:macro for d}}{${5:macro for shift x}}{${6:macro for shift y}}

macros.name: pgfhorizontaltransformationadjustment
macros.doc: When you scale the length of a horizontal line by this factor in the current transformation, you compensate for the scaling.

macros.name: pgfidrefnextuse
macros.doc: This command assigns a system layer identifier (the identifier returned by \pgfsys@new@id) to the ⟨macro⟩, namely the one that will be used the next time \pgfuseid is used.

macros.name: pgfifidreferenced
macros.doc: If ⟨name⟩ has been referenced, ⟨then code⟩ is executed, otherwise ⟨else code⟩.

macros.name: pgfimage
macros.doc: Declares the image under the name pgflastimage and immediately uses it.

macros.name: pgfimage
macros.doc: Declares the image under the name pgflastimage and immediately uses it.

macros.name: pgflinewidth
macros.doc: You can access the current line width via the TeX dimension \pgflinewidth.

macros.name: pgflowlevel
macros.doc: This command concatenates the canvas transformation matrix with the coordinate transformation specified by ⟨transformation code⟩.

macros.name: pgflowlevelobj
macros.doc: This command creates a local {pgfscope}. Inside this scope, \pgflowlevel is first called with the argument ⟨transformation code⟩, then the ⟨code⟩ is inserted.

macros.name: pgflowlevelsynccm
macros.doc: This command concatenates the canvas transformation matrix with the current coordinate transformation matrix.

macros.name: pgfpatharc
macros.doc: This command appends a part of a circle (or an ellipse) to the current path.

arg.snippet: pgfpatharctoprecomputed{${1:center point}}{${2:start angle}}{${3:end angle}}{${4:end point}}{${5:x-radius}}{${6:y-radius}}{${7:ratio x-radius/y-radius}}{${8:ratio y-radius/x-radius}}

macros.name: pgfpathcircle
macros.doc: A shorthand for \pgfpathellipse applied to ⟨center⟩ and the two axis vectors (⟨radius⟩, 0) and (0, ⟨radius⟩).

macros.name: pgfpathclose
macros.doc: This command closes the current part of the path by appending a straight line to the start point of the current part.

macros.name: pgfpathcosine
macros.doc: This command appends a cosine curve in the interval [0, π/2] to the current path.

arg.snippet: pgfpathcurvebetweentime{${1:time t 1}}{${2:time t 2}}{${3:point p}}{${4:point s 1}}{${5:point s 2}}{${6:point q}}
pgfpathcurvebetweentimecontinue{${1:time t 1}}{${2:time t 2}}{${3:point p}}{${4:point s 1}}{${5:point s 2}}{${6:point q}}

macros.name: pgfpathcurveto
macros.doc: This command extends the current path with a Bézier curve from the last point of the path to ⟨coordinate⟩.

macros.name: pgfpathellipse
macros.doc: The effect of this command is to append an ellipse to the current path (if the path is not empty, a new part is started).

macros.name: pgfpathgrid
macros.doc: Appends a grid to the current path.

macros.name: pgfpathgrid
macros.doc: Appends a grid to the current path.

macros.name: pgfpathlineto
macros.doc: This command extends the current path in a straight line to the given ⟨coordinate⟩.

macros.name: pgfpathmoveto
macros.doc: This command expects a pgf-coordinate like \pgfpointorigin as its parameter. When the current path is empty, this operation will start the path at the given ⟨coordinate⟩.

macros.name: pgfpathparabola
macros.doc: This command appends two half-parabolas to the current path.

macros.name: pgfpathqcurveto
macros.doc: The quick version of the curve-to operation. The first support point is (s1x , s1y ), the second support point is (s2x , s2y ), and the target is (tx , ty ).

macros.name: pgfpathqlineto
macros.doc: The quick version of the line-to operation.

macros.name: pgfpathqmoveto
macros.doc: Either starts a path or starts a new part of a path at the coordinate (⟨x dimension⟩, ⟨y dimension⟩).

macros.name: pgfpathquadraticcurveto
macros.doc: This command works like \pgfpathcurveto, only it uses a quadratic Bézier curve rather than a cubic one. This means that only one support point is needed.

macros.name: pgfpathrectangle
macros.doc: Adds a rectangle to the path whose one corner is ⟨corner⟩ and whose opposite corner is given by ⟨corner⟩ + ⟨diagonal vector⟩.

macros.name: pgfpathrectanglecorners
macros.doc: Adds a rectangle to the path whose two opposing corners are ⟨corner⟩ and ⟨opposite corner⟩.

macros.name: pgfpointadd
macros.doc: Returns the sum vector ⟨v1⟩ + ⟨v2⟩.

arg.snippet: pgfpointarcaxesattime{${1:time t}}{${2:center}}{${3:0-degree axis}}{${4:90-degree axis}}{${5:start angle}}{${6:end angle}}

macros.name: pgfpointborderrectangle
macros.doc: This command returns a point that lies on the intersection of a line starting at the origin and going towards the point ⟨direction point⟩ and a rectangle whose center is in the origin and whose upper right corner is at ⟨corner⟩.

macros.name: pgfpointcurveattime

arg.snippet: pgfpointcurveattime{${1:time t}}{${2:point p}}{${3:point s 1}}{${4:point s 2}}{${5:point q}}

macros.doc: Yields a point that is on the Bézier curve from p to q with the support points s1 and s2 .

macros.name: pgfpointdiff
macros.doc: Returns the difference vector ⟨end⟩ − ⟨start⟩.

macros.name: pgfpointintersectionofcircles
macros.doc: This command returns the intersection of the two circles centered at p1 and p2 with radii r1 and r2 . If ⟨solution⟩ is 1, the first intersection is returned, otherwise the second one is returned.

macros.name: pgfpointintersectionoflines
macros.doc: This command returns the intersection of a line going through p and q and a line going through s and t. If the lines do not intersection, an arithmetic overflow will occur.

macros.name: pgfpointlineatdistance
macros.doc: Yields a point that is located ⟨distance⟩ many units away from the start point in the direction of the end point.

macros.name: pgfpointnormalised
macros.doc: This command returns a normalised version of ⟨point⟩, that is, a vector of length 1pt pointing in the direction of ⟨point⟩.

macros.name: pgfpointorigin
macros.doc: Yields the origin.

macros.name: pgfpointpolar
macros.doc: Yields a point location given in polar coordinates.

macros.name: pgfpointpolarxy
macros.doc: This command is similar to the \pgfpointpolar command, but the ⟨radius⟩ is now a factor to be interpreted in the xy-coordinate system. This means that a degree of 0 is the same as the x-vector of the xy-coordinate system times ⟨radius⟩ and a degree of 90 is the y-vector times ⟨radius⟩.

macros.name: pgfpointscale
macros.doc: Returns the vector ⟨factor⟩⟨coordinate⟩.

macros.name: pgfpointspherical
macros.doc: This command yields a point “on the surface of the earth” specified by the ⟨longitude⟩ and the ⟨latitude⟩.

macros.name: pgfpointtransformed
macros.doc: Applies current transformation matrix to {⟨point⟩} (x, y) and returns a transformed point (ax + cy + s, bx + dy + t).

macros.name: pgfpointtransformednonlinear
macros.doc: Works like \pgfpointtransformed, but also applies the current nonlinear transformation; that is, it first applies the current linear transformation and then the current nonlinear transformations.

macros.name: pgfpointxy
macros.doc: Yields a point that is situated at sx times the x-vector plus sy times the y-vector.

macros.name: pgfpointxyz
macros.doc: Yields a point that is situated at sx times the x-vector plus sy times the y-vector plus sz times the z-vector.

macros.name: pgfpoptype
macros.doc: Restores the most recent type from the internal global stack of types.

macros.name: pgfpushtype
macros.doc: Pushes the current type on an internal global stack.

macros.name: pgfqbox
macros.doc: This command inserts a TeX box into a {pgfpicture} by “escaping” to TeX, inserting the box number ⟨box number⟩ at the origin, and then returning to the typesetting the picture.

macros.name: pgfqboxsynced
macros.doc: This command works similarly to the \pgfqbox command. However, before inserting the text in ⟨box number⟩, the current coordinate transformation matrix is applied to the current canvas transformation matrix (is it “synced” with this matrix, hence the name).

macros.name: pgfqpoint
macros.doc: This command does the same as \pgfpoint, but ⟨x⟩ and ⟨y⟩ must be simple dimensions like 1pt or 1cm.

macros.name: pgfqpointxy
macros.doc: This command does the same as \pgfpointxy, but ⟨sx⟩ and ⟨sy⟩ must be simple numbers without unit, like 1.234 or 5.0.

macros.name: pgfrdfabout
macros.doc: Adds the rdf attribute about="⟨text⟩" to the next id scope (please see the rdfa specification for details on the semantics of about in the context of the resource description framework).

macros.name: pgfrealjobname
macros.doc: Tells pgf the real name of your job.

macros.name: pgfresetboundingbox
macros.doc: Resets the picture’s bounding box.

macros.name: pgfsetadditionalshadetransform
macros.doc: This command allows you to specify an additional transformation that should be applied to shadings when the \pgfshadepath command is used.

macros.name: pgfsetarrowsstart
macros.doc: Sets the arrow tip kind used at the start of a (possibly curved) path.

macros.name: pgfsetbaseline
macros.doc: This command specifies a y-coordinate of the picture that should be used as the baseline of the whole picture.

macros.name: pgfsetbaselinepointnow
macros.doc: This command specifies the baseline indirectly, namely as the y-coordinate that the given ⟨point⟩ has when the command is called.

macros.name: pgfsetbeveljoin
macros.doc: Sets the line join to a bevel join.

macros.name: pgfsetblendmode
macros.doc: Sets the blend mode to one of the values described in Section 23.3.

macros.name: pgfsetbuttcap
macros.doc: Sets the line cap to a butt cap.

macros.name: pgfsetcolor
macros.doc: Sets both the stroke and fill color.

macros.name: pgfsetcornersarced
macros.doc: This command causes all subsequent corners to be replaced by little arcs.

macros.name: pgfsetdash

arg.snippet: pgfsetdash{${1:list of even length of dimensions}}{${2:phase}}

macros.doc: Sets the dashing of a line.

macros.name: pgfseteorule
macros.doc: Dictates that the even-odd rule is used in subsequent fillings in the current TeX scope.

macros.name: pgfsetfading
macros.doc: This command sets the graphic state parameter “fading” to a previously defined fading ⟨name⟩.

macros.name: pgfsetfillcolor
macros.doc: Sets the color used for filling paths to ⟨color⟩.

macros.name: pgfsetfillopacity
macros.doc: Sets the opacity of filling operations.

macros.name: pgfsetfillpattern
macros.doc: This command specifies that paths that are filled should be filled with the “color” by the pattern ⟨name⟩.

macros.name: pgfsetinnerlinewidth
macros.doc: This command sets the width of the inner line.

macros.name: pgfsetinnerstrokecolor
macros.doc: This command sets the ⟨color⟩ that is to be used when the inner line is stroked.

macros.name: pgfsetlayers
macros.doc: This command tells pgf which layers will be used in pictures.

macros.name: pgfsetlinewidth
macros.doc: This command sets the line width for subsequent strokes (in the current pgfscope).

macros.name: pgfsetmiterjoin
macros.doc: Sets the line join to a miter join.

macros.name: pgfsetmiterlimit
macros.doc: Sets the miter limit to ⟨miter limit factor⟩.

macros.name: pgfsetnonzerorule
macros.doc: Dictates that the nonzero winding number rule is used in subsequent fillings in the current TeX scope.

macros.name: pgfsetrectcap
macros.doc: Sets the line cap to a square cap.

macros.name: pgfsetroundcap
macros.doc: Sets the line cap to a round cap.

macros.name: pgfsetroundjoin
macros.doc: Sets the line join to a round join.

macros.name: pgfsetshortenstart
macros.doc: This command will shortened the start of every stroked path by the given dimension.

macros.name: pgfsetstrokecolor
macros.doc: Sets the color used for stroking lines to ⟨color⟩, where ⟨color⟩ is a LaTeX color like red or black!20!red.

macros.name: pgfsetstrokeopacity
macros.doc: Sets the opacity of stroking operations.

macros.name: pgfsettransform
macros.doc: Reinstalls a coordinate transformation matrix that was previously saved using \pgfgettransform.

macros.name: pgfsettransformentries
macros.doc: Reinstalls a coordinate transformation matrix that was previously saved using the storage command \pgfgettransformentries.

macros.name: pgfsetxvec
macros.doc: Sets that current x-vector for usage in the xyz-coordinate system.

macros.name: pgfshadecolortocmyk
macros.doc: This command takes ⟨color name⟩ as input, converts it to cmyk and stores the color’s cyan/magenta/yellow/black components real numbers between 0.0 and 1.0 separated by spaces.

macros.name: pgfshadecolortogray
macros.doc: This command takes ⟨color name⟩ as input converts it to grayscale and stores the color’s value as a real number between 0.0 and 1.0.

macros.name: pgfshadecolortorgb
macros.doc: This command takes ⟨color name⟩ as input, converts it to rgb and stores the color’s red/green/blue components real numbers between 0.0 and 1.0 separated by spaces (which is exactly what you need if you want to push it on a stack) in ⟨macro⟩.

macros.name: pgftext
macros.doc: This command will typeset ⟨text⟩ in normal TeX mode and insert the resulting box into the {pgfpicture}.

macros.name: pgftext
macros.doc: This command will typeset ⟨text⟩ in normal TeX mode and insert the resulting box into the {pgfpicture}.

arg.snippet: pgftransformarcaxesattime{${1:time t}}{${2:center}}{${3:0-degree axis}}{${4:90-degree axis}}{${5:start angle}}{${6:end angle}}

macros.name: pgftransformarrow
macros.doc: Shifts coordinates to the end of the line going from ⟨start⟩ to ⟨end⟩ with the correct rotation.

macros.name: pgftransformationadjustments
macros.doc: This command computes “adjustments” for the current transformation matrix so that even when you install a transformation matrix that scales everything by a certain factor, you can still draw something of “an absolute size”.

macros.name: pgftransformcm
macros.doc: Applies the transformation matrix given by a, b, c, and d and the shift ⟨point⟩ to coordinates (in addition to any previous transformations already in force).

macros.name: pgftransforminvert
macros.doc: Replaces the coordinate transformation matrix by a coordinate transformation matrix that “exactly undoes the original transformation”.

macros.name: pgftransformlineattime
macros.doc: Shifts coordinates by a specific point on a line at a specific time.

macros.name: pgftransformnonlinear
macros.doc: This command adds the ⟨transformation code⟩ to the list of non-linear transformations currently in force.

macros.name: pgftransformreset
macros.doc: Resets the coordinate transformation matrix to the identity matrix.

macros.name: pgftransformresetnontranslations
macros.doc: This command sets the a, b, c, and d part of the coordinate transformation matrix to a = 1, b = 0, c = 0, and d = 1.

macros.name: pgftransformrotate
macros.doc: Rotates coordinates counterclockwise by ⟨angles⟩ given in degrees.

macros.name: pgftransformscale
macros.doc: Scales coordinates by ⟨factor⟩.

macros.name: pgftransformshift
macros.doc: Shifts coordinates by ⟨point⟩.

macros.name: pgftransformtriangle
macros.doc: This command transforms the coordinate system in such a way that the triangle given by the points ⟨a⟩, ⟨b⟩ and ⟨c⟩ lies at the coordinates (0, 0), (1pt, 0pt) and (0pt, 1pt).

macros.name: pgftransformxscale
macros.doc: Scales coordinates by ⟨factor⟩ in the x-direction.

macros.name: pgftransformxshift
macros.doc: Shifts coordinates by ⟨dimension⟩ along the x-axis.

macros.name: pgftransformxslant
macros.doc: Slants coordinates by ⟨factor⟩ in the x-direction. Here, a factor of 1 means 45◦ .

macros.name: pgftransformyslant
macros.doc: Slants coordinates by ⟨factor⟩ in the y-direction.

macros.name: pgfuseid
macros.doc: You call \pgfuseid{⟨id⟩} to choose an id, which is a normal string.

macros.name: pgfuseimage
macros.doc: Inserts a previously declared image into the normal text.

macros.name: pgfusepathqclip
macros.doc: Clips all subsequent drawings against the current path.

macros.name: pgfusepathqfill
macros.doc: Fills the path without further ado.

macros.name: pgfusepathqfillstroke
macros.doc: Fills and then strokes the path without further ado.

macros.name: pgfusepathqstroke
macros.doc: Strokes the path without further ado.

macros.name: pgfusetype
macros.doc: Sets the type used for the referencing of graphic objects for the current scope to ⟨type⟩ or, if ⟨type⟩ starts with a dot, appends ⟨type⟩ to the current type.

envs.name: pgfidscope
envs.doc: Creates a graphic scope that will have the id last used with \pgfuseid attached to, provided such an id was set and was not already used with another object.

envs.name: pgfinterruptboundingbox
envs.doc: This environment temporarily interrupts the computation of the bounding box and sets up a new bounding box.

envs.name: pgfinterruptpath
envs.doc: This environment can be used to temporarily interrupt the construction of the current path.

envs.name: pgfonlayer
envs.doc: Using the {pgfonlayer} environment, you can tell pgf that certain commands should, instead, be added to the given layer.

envs.name: pgfscope
envs.doc: Inside a {pgfpicture} you can use a {pgfscope} environment to keep changes of the graphic state local to that environment.
